rows.27:12b14:
But there was nobody in there.
Instead, big letters had been scrawled across the wall.
In rough handwriting, it said
"Go to the third floor."
Just like that.
The only ones who'd pull something like this were those two.
They really were trying to scare the rest of them.
He got a little angry.
Then he decided to go up to the third floor.{p}
rows.27:12c38:
As he climbed the stairs, wouldn't you know it, he heard snickering from somewhere above.
It was them.
He wasn't going to be satisfied until he'd given them a piece of his mind.
He charged up the last few steps in one go.
And he shouted:{p}
rows.27:12cfc:
"Knock it off☆"

The feeling that someone was there, which he'd had until then, had vanished without a trace.
Even though he hadn't heard anyone running off.
Only then did he realize he'd come all the way up to the third floor.
Come to think of it, Hanako-san was supposed to haunt the restroom on this floor, wasn't she?
He broke out in goosebumps all over.{p}
rows.27:12e2c:
On the wall in front of him, a whole crowd of skull crests had surfaced.
He was startled, of course.
But they weren't skulls.
They looked just like them, but they were only stains on the wall.
Apparently they were shaped like human faces, so he'd mistaken them.
"Oh, is that all..."
Just as he let out a sigh.{p}
rows.27:12f3c:
With a skittering rustle, the stains squirmed.
The skulls sat up, slow and heavy, as if they'd been buried in the wall.{p}
rows.27:13064:
When they reached the stairs, the skulls went rolling up them, see.
He followed them, nervously.
Because he wanted to know where the skulls were headed.
Roll, roll, roll... up the stairs the skulls went.
And before long, they made it all the way to the third floor.{p}
rows.27:13148:
But it seemed the skulls' parade wasn't over yet.
They went rolling off down the hallway.{p}
rows.27:131a8: Just then, he suddenly heard a scream.{p}
rows.27:131d8:
At the same moment, the skulls in front of him vanished, just like that.
Had it been a hallucination...?{p}
rows.27:1322c:
He tried going up the stairs.
He figured that, on some whim, they might have picked the restroom one floor up.{p}
rows.27:132a8:
But the restroom light was off.
It looked like it wasn't the second floor after all.{p}
rows.27:132fc: That left the first floor and the third. What should he do?
rows.27:13324: Go back to the first floor
rows.27:13330: Try going up to the third floor
rows.27:13354:
He decided to go back to the first floor.
After all, the restroom closest to the classroom was the best bet, right?{p}
rows.27:133b8:
He decided to go up to the third floor.
That meant walking the creaking hallway back to the stairs again.{p}
rows.27:1340c:
He didn't open it.
The door opened all by itself.{p}
rows.27:1346c:
Standing startlingly close was a woman with a bobbed haircut.
She was wearing a sailor uniform soaked in blood.
Her eyes flashed for an instant inside a white mask.
And then she wrapped him in a tight embrace.
She pressed her head hard against his neck, and he couldn't help arching his back.
That leaves you looking straight up at the ceiling, right?
And so he saw them.{p}
rows.27:13584:
A whole crowd of women, stuck to the ceiling like geckos.
Short-haired ones, ones in braids, all kinds of women in blood-soaked sailor uniforms and white masks, clinging up there.
They were staring down at him.
He opened his throat to scream, and in a flash the woman bit it clean through.
As his blood sprayed up, he was thinking.{p}
rows.27:136b0:
Those small black creatures that had been carrying the three of them... maybe they were those skull stains...
Maybe they were bringing food to these women. That's what he thought.{p}
rows.27:13768:
Why say that now, after all this?
We're friends, aren't we?
We stick together, in good times and bad, right?
I already think of you as my best friend.
That's why I want you to solve the mystery of Hanako-san.
Can't you understand how I feel, as your best friend?
So it's okay, isn't it?
Let's go.
Right?
...Will you nod for me?{p}
rows.27:138f4:
Right, of course.
You're someone who doesn't want to go to the restroom, aren't you?
...Fine, I get it.
I get it perfectly.
Even after I've set everything up so nicely for you, you still won't go near a restroom.
Actually, I've had my eye on you this whole time.
You're kind of famous in some circles, you know.
Didn't you know that?{p}
rows.27:139f4:
I overheard some first-years talking about it.
They said you never, ever go to the restroom.
I thought, no way, that's ridiculous.
But it sounded interesting.
So I've been curious about you ever since.
And it turns out... you really don't go, do you?
I asked your classmates, and they say you don't go even once a day.
That's just not natural, no matter how you look at it.
And even now, when it's for your own project, you come out saying you won't go to the restroom.{p}
rows.27:13b74:
...But you know, I've figured it out.
You hate restrooms, don't you?
The smell in there, the air, or maybe the tiles or whatever they're made of. You can't stand them, can you?
That's how I figured it out.
You're not human.
If you were human, you'd always need the restroom.
You couldn't possibly loathe it that much.
So what are you?
An alien, maybe?{p}
rows.27:13d3c:
"You've disguised yourself very well.
But you can't fool my eyes."
He came closer.
His knife stayed {f:raised|raised}.
"I've tried dogs and cats, but I wonder what an alien's body looks like inside."
{f:What did he just say|What is he saying}?
Is this guy {f:even in his right mind|even sane}?
{f:Me|Me}, an alien?
Just because I don't go to the restroom, he'd been thinking that about me?
To tell the truth, it {f:wasn't as if I never went|isn't as if I never go} at all.
It's just my constitution; I go less often than normal people, that's all...
No, this {f:was|is} no time to argue about that.
What {f:was he going|is he going} to do★
{f:He must have read|Maybe he read} the look on {f:my|my} face.{p}
rows.27:13fb8:
Hosoda grinned.
"I'm going to dissect you.
Don't worry, it'll be over soon."
His eyes weren't sane.
"S-Somebody!"
A scream burst out of my mouth before I knew it.
"Hel..."{p}
rows.27:14070: Before I could finish, an arm shot out and {f:I|I} was shoved to the floor.{p}
rows.27:140bc:
Hosoda climbed on top of me, straddling me.
"It's okay, it's okay."{p}
rows.27:14174:
I couldn't tell if it was heat or pain.
Through my blurring vision I saw Hosoda, spattered with my green blood, grinning.
"Just as I thought."
{f:I|I} cursed myself.
The mission {f:was a failure|had failed}.
How could I slip up like this...{p}Bitterly regretting that I would die on this faraway alien planet, {f:I|I} slowly closed my eyes.{p}
rows.27:142f4:
Hosoda's fingers clamped down hard on my shoulder.
"I won't let you go home."
A smile that gave off something dangerous.
Because his eyes weren't smiling.
Between his narrowed lids, silver-white pupils were glinting.
This isn't Hosoda★
"Who are you...?"
My voice came out hoarse.
"Since when..."
At that, Hosoda(?)'s smile grew wider.
"Who'd have thought you'd stay fooled right to the very end?
It's a little early, but let's finish this here..."{p}
rows.27:14474:
As he said it, the skin of his face came sloughing off with a wet slop.
From beneath gentle Hosoda's face, huge goggling eyeballs emerged.
I remembered seeing something like it in the science room, long ago.
The muscle diagram on the anatomical model.
It looked just like that.
The thing was making a low chuckling sound in its throat.
It was laughing, watching me cower.{p}
rows.27:14588:
From somewhere it produced a white mask like a Noh mask, and pressed it onto its face.
The pure white, uncanny face came close to mine.
"This is me... the one who dwells in the old school building."
It whispered in my ear.
"I caught this one as he was leaving the classroom and took his skin.

Hosoda's skin★
Then Hosoda is...
I felt dizzy.
As I swayed, the thing caught me in its arms.
"Those who have the gift, yet cannot use it.

I was fading.
What on earth is happening to me?{p}As I slowly crumpled, its last words reached my ears.
"As the very finest food..."{p}
rows.27:147ec:
"Let's just go back."
When I said that, Hosoda nodded, looking relieved.
"Yeah.
Yeah, you're right."
He eagerly started to head back.
But then.{p}
rows.27:14888:
There was nothing in front of us.
The hallway floorboards ended right at our feet.
Before us spread a darkness like outer space.
"This is... th-this is a hallucination, right?"
Hosoda took a step forward.
But there was no such thing as an 'invisible floor.'
"Waaah!"
I yanked Hosoda back as he lost his footing.{p}
rows.27:149a4:
The momentum sent both of us tumbling over.
"No way... is there really no way back?"
Hosoda's voice was tearful.
But there was nothing I could do.
I felt like crying myself.
Now there was only one way left for us to go.
I steeled myself and opened my mouth.{p}
rows.27:14a98:
We'd come this far; surely that was enough.
That's what I thought.
I quietly backed away.
But just then.{p}
rows.27:14b18:
Knock... knock... knock...
The sound of knocking echoed.
It wasn't me.
It wasn't Hosoda, or anyone else, either.
Anyone else...?
With a start, I looked at the door.{p}
rows.27:14bb0:
Knock... knock... knock...
The knocking was coming from the other side of the door!
No doubt about it.
There's something in there.
"L-Let's just go home!"{p}
rows.27:14c34:
I was supposed to knock three times, right?
Just as I'd been told, I tried knocking three times.
Knock... knock... knock...
An answer...?
Knock... knock... knock...
An answer came back.
No doubt about it.
There's something in there!
"Stop it!
That's enough!
Let's go home, {a}!"
Hosoda's face was deathly pale.{p}
rows.27:14d64:
Just then, I was suddenly yanked upward with tremendous force.
"Waaaaaaaah!"
As if up and down had been flipped, I was slammed against the ceiling.
My arms and legs wouldn't move the way I wanted.{p}
rows.27:14e28:
I called out desperately to Hosoda, who was looking up at me.
"Help me!
Please, help...!"
But Hosoda shook his head.
"No. I won't."
I couldn't believe my ears.{p}
rows.27:14ecc:
"Well, you turned me down when I asked you to be my friend, didn't you?
And when I asked anyway, you even made that put-upon face."
Hosoda seemed to be enjoying this, somehow.
"Th-That's not true!"
"You see, I never forget being hurt. Not as long as I live.
I didn't expect things to turn out like this, but now maybe you'll understand the pain in my heart."
Through my back, I felt the ceiling undulate.
It twisted a little, and a split opened up like a huge mouth.
I didn't need to look to know.
That mouth was slowly opening wide.
"I understand!
I'm sorry, it was my fault.
Please forgive me!"
I was drenched in sweat from head to toe.
Hosoda smiled at me, sweating as I was.
"Not a chance."{p}
rows.27:1514c:
Behind me, the split gaped wide open.
The giant mouth in the ceiling swallowed me whole.{p}
rows.27:151a4: In the very last instant, I saw Hosoda walking out of the restroom.{p}
rows.27:151dc:
There was no way I could save him.
Even if I reached up, I couldn't reach the ceiling.
There was nothing at all I could do.
I'll just run.
I started to leave the restroom.
"{a}★"
I heard Hosoda's anguished cry.
"I'm sorry!"
Shouting that, I tried to dash out.
But my legs wouldn't move.
Not only that.{p}
rows.27:15314:
"Whoa★"
Suddenly my body floated up into the air.{p}
rows.27:1534c:
I was slammed up right next to Hosoda.
The impact squeezed the air out of my lungs.
I choked in spite of myself.
As I coughed, someone grabbed my shoulder.{p}
rows.27:153f0:
"How could you, {a}!"
Hosoda's eyebrows were raised in fury as he glared at me.
"You were going to abandon me and go home!"
It was a frightening face, like nothing I'd ever seen on him.
He might hit me.
But just then, Hosoda's gaze shifted past me, to something behind me.
His face twisted in terror.
"Ah... ah... ah..."
As if he'd forgotten how to speak, Hosoda just kept moaning.{p}
rows.27:15548: I followed his gaze and turned around.{p}
rows.27:15610:
The door of the second stall from the back stood open, and a masked girl was standing in it.
Suddenly, her voice echoed directly inside my head.
"You, or that one... which shall I choose?"
Her eyes were looking straight at me.
Me, and that one...?
Did she mean Hosoda?
"Which shall I choose?"
The voice echoed again.
She seemed to be thinking it over, but it also felt as if she was asking me.{p}Should I say something?
rows.27:157ac:
I hurriedly opened my mouth.
"Choose that one! Choose Hosoda!"
"{a}★
How could you..."
Hosoda's body came away from the ceiling.{p}
rows.27:1583c:
He hit the floor with a heavy thud.
"Ugh!"
The girl stood beside the groaning Hosoda.
She held out a slender hand.
"Get up."
Again, the voice echoed in my head.
But this time it seemed to be meant for Hosoda, not me.
Hosoda took her hand and stood up.
The eyes beneath the mask smiled.
"Just as that one said, I shall take you as my consort."
Consort?
Before I could think about what the word meant, the girl looked up at me again.
"The one left over is my gift to you.
Do with that one as you please."
Hearing that, Hosoda's face lit up.{p}
rows.27:15a44:
He looked up at me and smirked.
"So that's how it is."
I stared at him, wide-eyed.
I forced myself to swallow.
"H-Hosoda...?"
"{a}, you've abandoned me twice now, haven't you?
Even I have my limits, you know."
Hosoda was brimming with confidence, like a different person from a moment ago.
He must have been sure he wasn't going to be the one killed.
Did he mean to make his home in this old school building restroom, with the masked girl?
Hosoda nodded with a smile.
"You'll pay for betraying me with your life."{p}
rows.27:15c3c: The moment he said it, blood spurted from my neck.{p}
rows.27:15c70:
I hurriedly opened my mouth.
"I don't know what you're planning, but just choose me★"
Earlier, in a moment of weakness, I'd nearly abandoned Hosoda.
Hosoda called me his friend. I couldn't betray him any more than I already had.
Hosoda trembled.
"{a}.
You really are..."
Then he looked at the girl.
"No, take me!
{a} is my friend."

I felt the girl smile beneath her mask.
"Then both of you, is it?"

Its surface turned soft, and our bodies were sucked into it.

Hosoda flailed his arms and legs.{p}
rows.27:15ea8:
"No!
I take it back, stop!
Just take {a} alone☆"

The girl's voice spoke, and the ceiling turned springy again.
But Hosoda alone kept sinking, deeper and deeper.{p}
rows.27:15f84:
"No! I don't want this!
Somebody help me!
rows.27:15fd8:
The ceiling swallowed his struggling hands and rippled for an instant with a soft slosh.
After that, there was no sign of Hosoda at all.{p}
rows.27:16048:
The masked girl chuckled deep in her throat.
"By now you have learned how vile humans are.
Why not cut ties with such filthy things for good...?"
Behind the slits of her mask, her eyes gave off a sticky gleam.
But it didn't feel unpleasant at all...
Before I knew it, I was holding out my hand.
"I'll go.......... with you."
Her cold fingers closed around my hand.
I'd had enough of this grimy, filthy world.{p}I will live here.
In an eternity of time, set solid like jelly.{p}
rows.27:16238:
"I can't abandon my family.

I do feel bad for Hosoda.

Hosoda had gone deathly pale.
It seemed he couldn't even speak anymore.{p}
rows.27:16394:
When I came to, I was standing on the same restroom floor as before.
Hosoda was standing beside me too, looking dazed.
"I no longer need that one's life, nor your family's.

rows.27:1650c: As I stood there dumbfounded, my neck was suddenly squeezed tight.{p}
rows.27:16564:
"Ho... so... da...?"

"How dare you abandon me.

He squeezed without mercy, and my consciousness began to fade.
I tried to tear his hands away, but I had no strength left.
Slowly sinking into the abyss of death, I finally understood the masked girl's words.
The thing she'd obtained, as precious as a life...{p}It was Hosoda's sanity, and the trust between us.{p}
